postApprovalDeltas.evidence: 184 new mentions, all landing on the core registry (Democratic Party and Republican Party both being core-registry canonicals) and all via the alias-ruling mechanism. No entity ROWS created: both party canonicals already existed. Building this ruling also found and fixed a real gap in apply-entities.mjs's shared alias-matching regex: a leading   cannot match immediately before punctuation (the same reason a trailing   cannot match after it, which the file already handled) and a self-delimited bracket alias needs no trailing guard at all, since its own closing bracket is the boundary — without both fixes the ruling matched zero of its 103+7 named posts, a silent no-op the QA gate did not catch on its own (the fix is symmetric and additive: verified no other alias in the corpus starts or ends with punctuation, so no existing ruling's behaviour changed).
